subject: Model adaptation opt-out + prompt/response custody — evidence path
messages:
From: Kelly Santos <kelly@lumina.ai>
To: Ethan Park <ethan_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Lumina Therapeutics Legal <legal@lumina.ai>
Date: Thu, 30 Jul 2026 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Model adaptation opt-out and proof of non-adaptive processing

Hi Ethan,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency and routing controls look great. Before we move forward with a pilot, Legal needs an operational path to show Lumina's data won't be used to adapt or improve models. They are not asking for a contractual "no-training" clause yet, but they want an evidence package and a clear operational commitment for the pilot.

Key asks from Legal:
- A concise statement of how Redwood prevents model updates from customer inputs during the pilot (what's actually turned off).
- Logs or an evidence matrix showing which subprocessors touch request payloads and where data is stored/processed.
- Residency constraints for any intermediate storage (KV cache, batching queues).
- A simple runbook we can execute with them during onboarding to verify the non-adaptive setting.

Attachments: we attached Lumina's proposed DPA redline (lumina-dpa-redline.docx).

Can you confirm what's the minimum evidence set we can provide quickly and what operational changes the pilot needs? Also, any standard phrasing we can include in an addendum (DocuSign) would help speed procurement.

Best,
Kelly
Head of Product Security
Lumina Therapeutics

From: Ethan Park <ethan_park@redwood.com>
To: Kelly Santos <kelly@lumina.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Jul 2026 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Model adaptation opt-out and proof of non-adaptive processing

Hi Kelly — thanks, and glad the demo helped. Short answer: we can provide an "adaptation opt-out" operational mode for pilots plus an evidence bundle that aligns with what Legal asks for. Below is a pragmatic plan that we can turn into the addendum language and an onboarding runbook.

1) Operational mode (what we flip):
- Model adaptation disabled: customer inputs are marked as non-training and are excluded from any internal fine-tuning pipelines. Runtime flags: ADAPTATION=OFF at request router; KV cache can remain for latency but its contents are not dumped to training datasets.
- Ephemeral capture: set request retention to ephemeral (default 24h) and ensure no persistent storage for raw prompts.
- Onshore routing: for their pilot we can route inference to our us-east cluster only.

2) Evidence bundle (fast deliverables):
- Subprocessor snapshot (CSV) with hostnames, roles, and last-audit dates.
- Short operational note from Infra confirming ADAPTATION=OFF and code path ID.
- Sample logs (redacted) showing request tag "optout=true" and routing to us-east during a test window.
- A one-page runbook to verify settings via a guided call.

3) Addendum language (DocuSign-friendly):
- We can provide a 2-paragraph operational commitment that mirrors the above (operational mode + evidence). We avoid open-ended "no-training" legalese; instead we confirm "no model adaptation will occur from Customer Pilot Inputs during the Pilot Period."

Marissa — can you confirm we have a ready subprocessor snapshot and a small infra note we can sign off? Dylan — can you prepare a redacted sample log and a one-page runbook we can share?

I can draft the addendum language once we have confirmation. Happy to hop on a call with Legal tomorrow.

Cheers,
Ethan
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 30 Jul 2026 13:06:00 -07:00

On Thu, Jul 30, 2026 at 10:02 AM Ethan Park <ethan_park@redwood.com> wrote:
> Marissa — can you confirm we have a ready subprocessor snapshot and a small infra note we can sign off? Dylan — can you prepare a redacted sample log and a one-page runbook we can share?

Yes — attaching the snapshot and evidence matrix (evidence-matrix.xlsx) for ease. Highlights:
- Current subprocessors: s3-us-east (storage), redis-kv-cache (ephemeral cache), telemetry-proxy (aggregated metrics). Each row in the CSV shows what data they touch and whether data is persisted.
- Last audits: s3-us-east (2026-05-12), redis-kv-cache (2026-06-08), telemetry-proxy (2026-03-22).
- We can flag requests with header "X-Redwood-Adaptation: optout" which ensures downstream pipelines ignore the payload for training.

Dylan — is the sample log ready? If not, please draft a redacted excerpt that shows the optout header and the router decision.

I'll also draft the short infra note confirming the ADAPTATION=OFF code path and the us-east routing.

- Marissa
Product Privacy Lead
Redwood Inference

Attachment: evidence-matrix.xlsx

- We show real-time logs in a shared session with redaction; they can confirm the header, route, and decision field.
- We then share the subprocessor snapshot and infra note; if they want, we can arrange a brief third-party auditor call.

Next steps: Ethan to share the one-paragraph addendum for Lumina's DPA. Kelly — if that language looks OK, we can push a DocuSign addendum and schedule the onboarding verification session.
